payload.angle: The sourced legal guide to a Malta wedding for two Australians. The first screen answers 'can foreigners get married in Malta?' from the Public Registry (identita.gov.mt), not from tour operators. Then the Malta registration route (the expected opening, research confirms), the marry-in-Australia alternative, the Australian side nobody covers (documents, apostille, recognition, name change), and the invisible work of a Malta wedding week a Wedded Advisor coordinates. One short venue-shortlisting section catches venue-intent searchers without becoming a listicle.
serp_gaps_to_win: The AI Overview's legal block (no residency rule, RZ1 and RZ2, 6 weeks to 3 months, two witnesses) cites only UK tour operators and blogs. The first page that states these facts from identita.gov.mt and the Marriage Act wins the trust lane.
No ranking page covers the Australian side: documents from Australian registries, apostille, recognition under the Marriage Act 1961, passports name change.
No ranking page offers the marry-in-Australia, celebrate-in-Malta route.
Live Facebook and Reddit threads (2025 and 2026) ask the legal question; nobody answers it with sources.
Cost content is in GBP package prices with savings framing; an AUD-aware, planning-led page is absent.
